questions.question: What happens to the stored energy in a stretched elastic band or a compressed spring when it is released? Give an example.
questions.expected_answer: It is changed into movement energy, so something moves. For example, a released elastic band flies across the room, a jack-in-the-box spring pushes the clown up, or a bow straightens and makes an arrow fly.

questions.question: Explain how energy changes during a bungee jump.
questions.expected_answer: As the jumper falls, she gains movement energy. The cord stretches and slows her down, changing movement energy into stored energy in the cord. At the bottom, the cord is stretched most. Then it pulls back, releasing its stored energy as movement energy, which shoots her back up. Some energy becomes heat and sound, so each bounce is lower.

questions.question: Describe how a cotton-reel tractor works and how you would test the effect of the number of twists fairly.
questions.expected_answer: An elastic band through the reel is twisted by winding a pencil, storing energy. When released, the band untwists and turns the reel, so the tractor moves. To test fairly, use the same tractor, band and floor, and change only the number of twists, such as 10, 20 and 30, measuring how far it travels each time.
